# iproute_link_attachment (Resource)

Attaches a pre-existing network interface to a namespace and/or bridge without creating it. Moves the interface into the target network namespace (optional), enslaves it to a master bridge (optional) and brings it up. Reverses all of this on destroy. Use it to bridge a physical NIC or a container veth into a bridge declaratively.

This is the declarative replacement for the imperative `ip link set <dev> netns <ns> master <br> up` sequence. Unlike `iproute_link`, it never creates or destroys the interface itself — it only manages where the interface lives and what it is enslaved to. On destroy it reverses the placement: the interface is detached from its master, brought down, and returned to the provider's namespace.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Bridge an existing physical NIC into a bridge.
resource "iproute_link_attachment" "uplink" {
  name   = "eth1"
  master = iproute_link.br0.name
  up     = true
}

# Move a container's veth into a namespace and enslave it to a bridge there.
resource "iproute_link_attachment" "container_port" {
  name   = "veth-app"
  netns  = "docker:${docker_container.app.id}"
  master = "br0"
  up     = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the existing interface to attach.

### Optional

- `master` (String) Master bridge to enslave the interface to (resolved in the target namespace).
- `netns` (String) Target network namespace to move the interface into, using the same syntax as the provider's namespace argument (name, name:, pid:, path: or docker:). When unset, the interface stays in the provider's namespace and is only enslaved/brought up there.
- `up` (Boolean) Administrative state. Defaults to true.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
terraform import iproute_link_attachment.example <interface-name>
```
